lines.text: relationship between Christianity and idealism, and to-day
especially we should ponder these matters anew. Just now we
will only say, quite briefly: the gospel spells the rejection of
the world of the spirit if man sees in that world a structure
which he himself has raised, the expression of his own
creative power and perfection. But the gospel signifies the
confirmation of the world of the spirit, if man recognizes in
that world the divine authority under which he stands, and
if he does not attempt to hide the fact that he can never
satisfy the claim of this authority. And this not only in the
sense of his realizing that he is never yet what he should be,
but also in the sense of his realizing that he is always already
what he should not be. He is guilty, not only in the sense
that ever increasing obligations exceed the measure of his
fulfilment, but also in the sense that he has rendered himself
guilty by showing himself to be unworthy of these high
duties. He is constantly frustrated not only by the imperfec-
tion of all things earthly in which the ideal can never find
pure expression, but also by his own doing, by his own past
which makes him unclean in the face of the holy. His
conscience accuses him. He belongs to two worlds: his true
and better self belongs to the world of the spirit, but that
fact may not and cannot justify him or quieten the accusa-
tions of his conscience so long as he is bound to confess that
this his true self has not really become his own but ever
hovers before him as an unattained ideal. His empirical
ego is in fact the battle-ground of the struggle between the
powers of the spirit and the lower impulses. His ego is rent
in twain; it lacks unity and purity. It needs cleansing,
purification from the stains of the old man, emancipation from
its disharmonies, regeneration; in a word, it needs divine grace.
And it is just this which has become luminous for Paul in
the face of Jesus Christ: the grace of God which has made
him a new creature. "For it is the God who said, 'Let light
shine out of darkness'
who has shone in our hearts to give
the light of the knowledge of the glory of God in the face
of Christ."
